svg.aria-label: Two charts for the no-start tree. Left, starts then dies: that isn't the immobilizer's signature, because BMW describes a mismatch as crank-no-start and a deleted DME ignores the code, so look at the EWS only if 130 (0x82) or 66 (0x42) is stored, and after a confirmed delete not for a leftover 130 on its own. If it dies within about 3 seconds with the EML lamp on and won't restart, it's a throttle fault shutdown: read the faults 118 to 121 (0x76 to 0x79) for the throttle sensors, 60 and 61 (0x3C, 0x3D) for the pedal and 228 to 230 (0xE4 to 0xE6) for throttle control. If it dies when the prime would end, the pump isn't being held: the DME needs the engine-speed signal to keep K96 on, so check STAT_EKP_EIN with the engine running. If it dies at idle with no EML lamp: the idle actuator, leaks at the idle-air pipe, the adaptation, fuel pressure. If it runs only with the pump fuse pulled, then floods: an unseated terminal, so tug-test. Right, fault numbers: INPA prints decimal and the job documentation hex; 130 (0x82) is the immobilizer fault and 1 (0x01) the pump-relay fault that US software stores when K96 replaces the pump module. The harmless and the real fault 1 carry the same number, so tell them apart by what the car does: one prime with K96 clicking, 5.0 plus or minus 0.2 bar (BMW), the engine starting and running and STAT_MIL_EIN at 0 means the expected fault, so record it and do nothing; no prime, no pressure and K96 silent means a real pump-circuit fault; cranks without starting with all six injectors disabled is usually not the pump: in the 2002 325iT case it followed an immobilizer problem, so read 130 (0x82), 66 (0x42) and STAT_EWS3_FREIGABE first.
svg.text: Question
Expected: record it
Stop: fix before going on
Note
STARTS, THEN DIES
Not the immobilizer's signature: BMW describes a
mismatch as crank-no-start, and a deleted DME ignores the
code. Look at the EWS only if 130 (0x82) or 66 (0x42) is
stored, and after a confirmed delete not for a leftover 130 on
its own.
How does it die?

text.tspan: Within about 3 seconds, EML lamp on, won't restart:

svg.text: a throttle fault shutdown. Read the faults:
118–121 (0x76–0x79) throttle sensors,
throttle control. MotoIQ worked through throttle
sensor 1, the pedal, throttle sensor 2, the
synchronization and the actuator, suspecting low
charging voltage too.
When the prime would end: the pump isn't being
held. The DME needs the engine-speed signal to keep
K96 on; check STAT_EKP_EIN with the engine
running.
At idle, no EML lamp: the idle actuator, leaks at the
idle-air pipe, the adaptation, fuel pressure.

text.tspan: Runs only with the pump fuse pulled, then floods:

svg.text: an unseated terminal (in an E36 S54 swap, a ground at
X60003 pin 25). Tug-test.
FAULT 1: EXPECTED OR REAL?
Fault numbers: INPA prints decimal, the job documentation
hex. 130 (0x82), "EWS-Signalmanipulation", is the
immobilizer fault; 1 (0x01), "Relais Kraftstoffpumpe", the
pump fault US software stores when K96 replaces the pump
module.
Fault 1 stored: what does the car do?

text.tspan: clicks), 5.0 ± 0.2 bar (BMW), it starts and runs,

svg.text: STAT_MIL_EIN = 0: the expected fault. US software
misses its pump module. Record it; nothing to do.
No prime, no pressure, K96 silent: a real
pump-circuit fault. "Checks on the pump circuit" 1–3;
fuses F54 and F3; swap K96 with K19.

text.tspan: Cranks, won't start; all six injectors disabled:

svg.text: usually not the pump; in the 2002 325iT case it
followed an immobilizer problem. Read 130 (0x82),
66 (0x42) and STAT_EWS3_FREIGABE first
(Session 3).
